lemma minus_norm : ‖R.minus‖ ≤ (T-a)/2 := by
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ i, ‖((1-R.sign i)/2*R.weight i) • R.point i‖ := norm_sum_le _ _
findings.problem: plus_norm (495–508) and minus_norm (510–523) have the same 14-line proof, differing only in the sign in front of R.sign i. Both apply the triangle inequality for finite sums. Both prove nonnegativity of the coefficient by a case split on sign_eq with nlinarith. Both use norm_smul and point_norm to bound each term by its coefficient. Both rewrite the coefficient sum with sum_weight and sum_sign. A fix to one proof (for example the nlinarith case split or the simp_rw) has to be copied to the other by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add a general helper before `plus`, with n arbitrary and no signed-representation structure: `lemma norm_sum_smul_le_sum {ι} (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℝ) (p : ι → E) (hc : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i) (hp : ∀ i, ‖p i‖ ≤ 1) : ‖∑ i ∈ s, c i • p i‖ ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, c i`. Prove it with norm_sum_le, then sum_le_sum, using norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg and mul_le_of_le_one_right. Then add a signed-part lemma with a sign parameter ε, using hypothesis `hε : ε = 1 ∨ ε = -1`: `lemma part_norm : ‖∑ i, ((1 + ε * R.sign i)/2 * R.weight i) • R.point i‖ ≤ (T + ε * a)/2`. The coefficient nonnegativity is then a single `rcases R.sign_eq i, hε` case split, and the sum evaluation is one `rw [← sum_div, sum_add_distrib, ← mul_sum, ...]`. Either define plus and minus as the ε = 1 and ε = -1 instances, or prove `plus_norm` and `minus_norm` from `part_norm` with a short `simpa` that normalises `1 + (-1)*s` to `1 - s`. The statements of plus_norm, minus_norm and difference_mem stay unchanged.
findings.benefit: The nonnegativity, norm-bound and sum-evaluation reasoning is written once, so fixes and changes to plus/minus stay in one place. The generic helper `norm_sum_smul_le_sum` is also reusable outside this structure.

_ ≤ ‖a • zm‖ + ‖b • vm‖ := norm_add_le _ _
      _ = a * ‖zm‖ + b * ‖vm‖ := by
findings.problem: The second and third bullets of convex_aggregateSet (286–293 and 294–301) are identical 8-line calc chains. Each proves that a convex combination a•p + b•q of two vectors of norm ≤ C has norm ≤ C, once with C = A and once with C = B. Each runs norm_add_le, norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg, monotonicity, then add_mul/hab/one_mul. This is the convexity of a norm ball. The file already uses `convex_closedBall (0 : E) 1` elsewhere, in unitBall_eq_finite_convexHull_of_medians.
findings.proposed_change: Prove the two norm bounds with one shared fact. One option is `lemma norm_convex_comb_le {p q : E} {C a b : ℝ} (hp : ‖p‖ ≤ C) (hq : ‖q‖ ≤ C) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) : ‖a • p + b • q‖ ≤ C`. Prove it once with the existing calc, or by applying `convex_closedBall (0 : E) C` to the two points via `mem_closedBall_zero_iff`. The second and third bullets then become `exact norm_convex_comb_le hzp hvp ha hb hab` and `exact norm_convex_comb_le hzm hvm ha hb hab`. The same helper can be reused in the compactness/convexity arguments for the set S in aggregate_decomposition_of_support if needed.
findings.benefit: This removes about 8 duplicated lines of norm arithmetic and makes the convexity proof read as the three facts it checks (sum, plus-norm, minus-norm). It also isolates the one analytic step, so it is easier to maintain or replace with the Mathlib ball-convexity API.
